Let  
\[
C_{.95}\subset \mathbb R^2
\]
denote the plotted 95% confidence ellipse in the \((\beta_{15},\beta_{75})\)-plane.

A joint point null \(H_0:\,(\beta_{15},\beta_{75})=(a,b)\) is rejected at level \(0.05\) iff the point \((a,b)\) is outside the 95% ellipse.

For a one-parameter null such as \(H_0:\beta_{15}=a\), the null set is the vertical line  
\[
L_a=\{(a,y):y\in\mathbb R\}.
\]
Using the confidence-set/test duality, we reject iff this line does not intersect the ellipse. Similarly \(H_0:\beta_{75}=b\) corresponds to the horizontal line \(y=b\).

Boundary points are conventionally treated as “not rejected” at the 5% level.

---

## (1)

\[
H_0^1:\beta_{15}=-0.4
\]

Reject \(H_0^1\) iff the vertical line \(\beta_{15}=-0.4\) misses the ellipse.

\[
H_0^2:\beta_{75}=-0.4
\]

Reject \(H_0^2\) iff the horizontal line \(\beta_{75}=-0.4\) misses the ellipse.

\[
H_0^3:\beta_{15}=\beta_{75}=-0.4
\]

Reject \(H_0^3\) iff the point  
\[
(-0.4,-0.4)
\]
lies outside the ellipse.

Thus it is possible, for example, that both one-dimensional nulls are not rejected while the joint null is rejected, if the two lines intersect the ellipse but their intersection point lies outside the ellipse.

---

## (2)

\[
H_0^4:\beta_{15}=-0.2
\]

Reject iff the vertical line \(\beta_{15}=-0.2\) misses the ellipse.

\[
H_0^5:\beta_{75}=0.6
\]

Reject iff the horizontal line \(\beta_{75}=0.6\) misses the ellipse.

\[
H_0^6:\beta_{15}=-0.2,\ \beta_{75}=0.6
\]

Reject iff the point  
\[
(-0.2,0.6)
\]
lies outside the ellipse.

So the decision is determined geometrically by whether the relevant line or point intersects/lies in the ellipse.

---

## (3)

Let  
\[
p=(-0.6,0).
\]

The nulls are

\[
H_0^7:\beta_{15}=-0.6,
\qquad
H_0^8:\beta_{75}=0,
\qquad
H_0^9:(\beta_{15},\beta_{75})=(-0.6,0).
\]

If the joint null \(H_0^9\) is **not** rejected, then \(p=(-0.6,0)\) must lie inside the 95% confidence ellipse.

But \(p\) lies on both the vertical line \(\beta_{15}=-0.6\) and the horizontal line \(\beta_{75}=0\). Therefore, if \(p\) is inside the ellipse, both of those lines intersect the ellipse. Hence \(H_0^7\) and \(H_0^8\) would also not be rejected.

So, using the same confidence ellipse to test all three hypotheses, the stated outcome is impossible:

\[
\text{Reject }H_0^7,\ \text{reject }H_0^8,\ \text{but not reject }H_0^9
\]

cannot occur.

Equivalently, there is no modified ellipse for which the point \((-0.6,0)\) is inside the ellipse while both corresponding coordinate lines fail to intersect it.
